BRIDGE FINANCING — THE WINDOW MOST BROKERS MISS

Good morning,

We see it every week: a client is buying before they sell, and the broker scrambles to make traditional financing fit a timeline that was never going to work.

That's a bridge file. And it's one of the strongest deal types we fund.

Bridge financing is the right call when:
• Your client is purchasing a new property before their existing one closes
• A renovation or repositioning needs to happen before refinancing
• Timing matters more than the lowest rate
• The client has equity but needs liquidity now, not in 90 days

BROKER UPDATE

5 SIGNS A FILE BELONGS WITH A PRIVATE LENDER

Good morning,

If you're not sure whether to send a file to a bank, a B-lender, or a private lender like us — here's a quick filter we share with the brokers we work with most.

Send it to us if:

1. Timeline is the real constraint. The deal works financially but won't close fast enough through traditional channels.

2. The story doesn't fit a bank template. Self-employed, BFS, recently restructured, complex income — all fine for us, problematic for the bank.

3. Equity is strong but cash flow is tight (or vice versa). We underwrite the full picture, not a single ratio.

4. The file is unique. Construction draws, land servicing, mixed-use, unusual property type — these are normal conversations for us.

5. The client has been declined elsewhere — but the deal is still good. Most of our best files are deals that didn't fit somewhere else.

[ORANGE CALLOUT BOX]
If you're on the fence about whether a file is "private deal" material, send a one-paragraph summary. We'll tell you in hours whether we can structure it.

BROKER UPDATE

3 STRUCTURING MISTAKES THAT COST YOU DEALS

Good morning,

When a file falls apart at the private level, it's almost never the borrower. It's usually a small structuring decision that could have gone differently.

Mistake #1: Submitting incomplete on day one.
We'd rather have a one-paragraph summary with the basics than a perfectly polished package three days later. Speed beats polish.

Mistake #2: Pitching the wrong exit.
"Refinance with a bank in 12 months" only works if the client's income story improves. If it won't, that's a different conversation — and we can structure for it.

Mistake #3: Hiding the messy stuff.
Bankruptcy, judgments, recent restructuring — tell us upfront. We've underwritten around all of it. What kills a deal isn't the issue; it's finding out about it at the lawyer's office.

[ORANGE CALLOUT BOX]
The brokers we do the most volume with all do the same thing: they package files honestly, tell us the real story, and let us structure around it.
[/ORANGE CALLOUT BOX]

emails.preview: A simple framework for choosing the right structure.
emails.body:
BROKER UPDATE

EQUITY TAKE-OUT vs. REFINANCE — WHICH TO PITCH

Good morning,

A question we get from brokers regularly: when do you pitch a client an equity take-out versus a full refinance?

Pitch a full refinance when:
• The current 1st mortgage is at a rate worse than what's available today
• The client needs to restructure the whole debt picture
• Penalty math works in their favour
• They want a single payment going forward

Pitch an equity take-out (2nd mortgage) when:
• The existing 1st is at a low rate the client doesn't want to touch
• Penalty would be punishing
• The need is short-to-medium term (12-24 months)
• The exit is a defined event (sale, business liquidity event, refinance later)

[ORANGE CALLOUT BOX]
Quick rule of thumb: If preserving the existing 1st mortgage saves the client more than the cost of a 2nd, structure as a take-out. If not, refinance the whole thing. When in doubt, send us the file and we'll model both.
[/ORANGE CALLOUT BOX]

[DISCUSS YOUR NEXT DEAL]

BROKER UPDATE

HOW TO SET UP Q4 FOR YOUR STRONGEST QUARTER

Good morning,

Q4 is when the broker year is made or lost. Here's how the brokers we work with most are setting up for theirs.

Play 1: Audit your pipeline today. Pull every file in your CRM that's been sitting more than 30 days. Half of them belong with a private lender. Send them over.

Play 2: Reach out to every renewal in your book that's coming up before March. Bank renewals are getting tighter. Clients who got declined or down-graded are everywhere. Get ahead of it.

Play 3: Identify your 3 strongest centres of influence. Realtors, accountants, lawyers — three people who could feed you 2-3 deals each over Q4. Take them to coffee this week.

Where Richview fits: when one of those Q4 files needs to move in 48 hours, or doesn't fit the bank box, we're the call. Lock us in as your private option now, before the December scramble.
